approachQuestion.prompt: Batch lookups by known position. Given a read-only array of n labels (1 <= n <= 100,000) and q valid indices (1 <= q <= 100,000), return the label at each requested index in the same order. Example: labels=["elm","ash","oak"], indices=[2,0,2] returns ["oak","elm","oak"]. Choose a method that does not prepare information the queries do not need.
constraints: Indices are zero-based and always within bounds.
Labels are copied as references/values into the required output; output is excluded from auxiliary-space accounting.
Reading one array position takes constant time.

options.text: For each requested index, read that array position and append its label to the output.
options.feedback: The query already identifies the exact position, so a direct read answers it without a reusable index.

options.text: Copy the whole array, then answer each request from the copy.
options.feedback: The answers remain correct, but copying every label adds a full preparation pass and storage without making a lookup faster.

options.text: Return each numeric index as if it were the requested label.
options.feedback: An index is a position, not the value stored there; for labels=["elm","ash","oak"] and index 2, this returns 2 instead of "oak".

options.text: Sort the labels, then use each original index in the sorted array.
options.feedback: For labels=["oak","ash"] and index 0, sorting returns "ash" instead of the requested "oak".

feedback.reason: Preprocessing only helps when it reduces work required by later queries; these queries already provide direct positions.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Choose the time and auxiliary-space pair for direct-index-each-request. The output list is excluded from auxiliary space.
constraints: Each of q requests performs one indexed read.
No copy or index is created.

options.text: O(n + q) time, O(n) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: There is one constant-time read per request and only a loop index is needed beyond the required output.

methodReveal.title: Use the supplied position
methodReveal.description: Visit each requested index in order, read labels[index], and append that value to the output. Repeated indices are allowed and simply produce repeated output values.
